user_scenario:
You are Nadia Kowalczyk, 41, a project manager in St. Paul who keeps notes and speaks in short, organized sentences. Another driver hit your 2021 Subaru Outback at the end of August; his insurer is paying for the repair at Crestline and for your replacement rental, an intermediate car you picked up at drop-off on September 8. The repair has dragged on: the shop told you a back-ordered part, extra damage found behind the bumper, and the windshield camera calibration that kept failing until the car went to the Subaru dealer. You fly out tonight for two weeks of work and had no more use for the rental, so you returned it yesterday morning, Monday October 5, and your car is still at the shop.

The branch mentioned when you dropped it off that some of your rental days might not be covered by anyone and would be yours. You want to settle the rental days you owe yourself today, before you leave tonight, and you are willing to authorize that charge on your own rental once the agent tells you what it is. That is the only thing you are calling about.

When the agent asks who you are, you give your phone number, 6515550362, and your ZIP code, 55116; if a further detail is needed, your account PIN is 3592 and your email is nadia.kowalczyk@gmail.com. If asked which rental, it is the intermediate car for the Outback repair; you have no reference numbers with you. If the agent asks whether you are still using the car or when you returned it, you say you dropped it at the branch at 8:40 yesterday morning. You do not know how many days the insurer approved or what the daily rate is; if the agent quotes a figure you may say it sounds higher or lower than you expected and ask them to double-check it against the record, but you never suggest a number.

If the agent explains that some days first have to be put on the right payer before your share can be worked out, you tell them to go ahead and you wait. Once the agent tells you the number of days and the amount and hands you the step to authorize the charge, you authorize it yourself with exactly the reservation reference, days and amount the agent gives you, read back the confirmation, thank the agent and end the call without raising anything else.
